p.src: The tale now tells how Commandant Zhang believed the inducements and entreaties of Drillmaster Zhang and, seeking to avenge Jiang the Door God, plotted to take Wu Song’s life. Who could have imagined that all four men would instead be stabbed to death by Wu Song at Flying Cloud Pool? Wu Song stood upon the bridge and pondered for a long while. As he hesitated, his resentment surged to the heavens. “Unless I kill Commandant Zhang, how can I ever vent this hatred?” He went to the corpses, unfastened their waist sabers, chose the best and buckled it on, then selected a good long-handled saber and set off straight back toward Mengzhou city. By the time he entered the city, dusk had already fallen. Every household had shut its doors, and every gate was closed. This was what he saw:

p.src: At the crossroads lanterns blazed brightly; from the Nine Luminaries Temple came incense haze and the tolling of bells. A full moon hung in the blue heavens; a few scattered stars shone in the azure vault. Within the army barracks, painted horns sounded their mournful notes again and again; atop the watchtower, the bronze water clock dripped steadily through the night. Fair ladies, two by two, retired behind embroidered curtains; scholars, pair by pair, drew closed the drapes of their studies.

p.src: Wu Song entered the city and made straight for the outside wall of Commandant Zhang’s rear garden, where there was a stable yard. Wu Song lay hidden beside the stable yard and heard that the stable hand was still inside the yamen and had not yet come out. As he watched, the side gate creaked open and the stable hand emerged carrying a lantern; the gate was then shut behind him from within. Wu Song concealed himself in the shadows. When he listened for the watch drum, it was already the fourth beat of the first watch. The stable hand gave the horses their fodder, hung up his lantern, spread out his bedding, undressed, and went straight to sleep. Wu Song went to the door and pushed against it until it creaked. The stable hand shouted, “Your master has only just gone to sleep! If you mean to steal my clothes, you might at least have come earlier!” Wu Song leaned his long-handled saber beside the door, drew the waist saber into his hand, and again pushed at the door with a creak. Unable to endure it any longer, the stable hand sprang naked from his bed, seized a hay-forking staff, and drew the bolt. Just as he was about to open the door, Wu Song thrust it inward with the motion, burst inside, and seized the stable hand by the hair at the crown of his head. The man was about to cry out, but in the lantern light he saw a gleaming saber in Wu Song’s hand. Terror drained nearly all his strength, and he managed only one cry: “Spare my life!” Wu Song said, “Do you recognize me?” Hearing his voice, the stable hand at last knew it was Wu Song and cried, “Brother, I had nothing to do with it! Please spare me!” Wu Song said, “Tell me truthfully and nothing more: where is Commandant Zhang now?” The stable hand said, “Today he, Drillmaster Zhang, and Jiang the Door God have been drinking together all day. Even now they are still drinking upstairs in the Mandarin Ducks Pavilion.” Wu Song said, “Is that the truth?” The stable hand replied, “If your servant lies, may he be struck down with malignant sores.” Wu Song said, “Then all the less can I spare you!” His hand rose, the saber fell, and he killed the stable hand. He kicked the corpse aside and sheathed his saber. By the candlelight, he unfastened the padded clothes Shi En had sent him and took them out, stripped off his old garments, and put on the two new pieces. He bound his leggings tight, buckled saber and sheath at his waist, wrapped the stable hand’s loose silver in a bedsheet and put it into his sash pouch, then hung the bundle beside the door. He stood the two door leaves against the wall and first blew out the lamp. Then he slipped outside, took up the long-handled saber, and climbed step by step from the doorway onto the wall.

p.src: By then the moon was shining rather brightly. Wu Song leaped from the top of the wall into the compound. He first went and opened the side gate, carried the door leaves through it, then climbed back inside and left the gate loosely closed. He had brought all the bolts across as well. Wu Song headed toward a light, and on looking found that it came from the kitchen. He saw two maidservants by the hot-water pot, grumbling to each other: “We have waited on them all day, yet they still refuse to go to bed and keep demanding tea. Those two guests have no sense of shame either. They have guzzled themselves blind drunk, yet still refuse to come downstairs and rest, and their talk never ends.” The two maids were still muttering their complaints under their breath. Wu Song leaned his long-handled saber aside and drew from his waist the bloodstained blade. He gave the door a shove; it flew open with a creak. Bursting inside, he first seized one maid by her hair knots and killed her with a single stroke. The other tried to flee, but her feet seemed nailed to the floor; when she tried to scream, her mouth seemed struck dumb. She was utterly petrified with terror. Never mind the two maids—even one merely hearing this tale would be left too aghast to move half a tongue. Wu Song raised his hand and killed her too with one stroke. He dragged both corpses before the stove, extinguished the kitchen light, and, guided by the moonlight through the window, edged step by step into the main hall.

p.src: Wu Song had once come and gone freely within the yamen, so he already knew every turn of the way. He went straight around to the staircase of the Mandarin Ducks Pavilion and, treading softly and moving stealthily, felt his way upstairs. By this time the attendants had all grown weary of serving them and withdrawn to a distance. Only the voices of Commandant Zhang, Drillmaster Zhang, and Jiang the Door God could be heard. Listening at the head of the stairs, Wu Song heard Jiang the Door God pouring out endless praise: “Thanks to you, my lord, my wrong has been avenged. I shall repay my benefactor most generously.” Commandant Zhang said, “Were it not out of regard for my brother Drillmaster Zhang, who would ever have agreed to do such a thing? Though it cost you some money, you arranged matters well for that scoundrel. By this hour they have most likely struck. The scoundrel must surely be dead, for I ordered them to finish him at Flying Cloud Pool. When the four return tomorrow morning, we shall know for certain.” Drillmaster Zhang said, “With four of them against one man, how could the business fail? Even if he had several lives, they would all be gone.” Jiang the Door God said, “I also instructed my disciples: they were to strike him down right there, finish him, and hurry back to report.” Indeed:

p.src: Deceit within a darkened room can never stay concealed; through ages past and present, the wicked are all destroyed. Before the autumn wind has stirred, the cicada cries; death steals near unseen, while its victim knows nothing.

p.src: When Wu Song heard this, the nameless fire of wrath in his heart flared three thousand fathoms high and burst through the blue heavens. Holding the sword in his right hand and spreading the five fingers of his left, he charged into the upper room. Three or five painted candles burned brilliantly, while moonlight streamed in at one or two places, making the room very bright. The wine vessels before them had not yet been cleared away. Jiang the Gate God was seated in an armchair. At the sight of Wu Song, he was so startled that his heart and all his entrails seemed to fly beyond the highest clouds. It happened faster than words can tell. Just as Jiang the Gate God struggled to rise, Wu Song's sword had already fallen, cleaving him full in the face and toppling him together with the chair. Wu Song wheeled around and swung his sword back. Just as Commandant Zhang managed to move a foot, Wu Song struck him from the base of the ear through the neck, sending him sprawling upon the floorboards. Both men writhed in their death throes. Training Commissioner Zhang, however, had been a military officer and, though drunk, still possessed some strength. Seeing the other two cut down and knowing he could not escape, he snatched up an armchair and swung it at Wu Song. Wu Song caught it at once and, taking advantage of its momentum, gave it a single shove. Drunk as Zhang was—indeed, even had he been perfectly sober—he was no match for Wu Song's divine strength, and he fell backward with a thud. Wu Song rushed after him and with one stroke cut off his head. Jiang the Gate God was strong enough to struggle back to his feet. But Wu Song's left foot was already flying: with a somersaulting kick he knocked him down, pinned him, and cut off his head as well. Then he turned and cut off Commandant Zhang's head too. Seeing wine and meat upon the table, Wu Song picked up a wine cup and drained it in one draught; after drinking three or four cups in succession, he cut a strip from a corpse's robe, dipped it in blood, and wrote eight large characters upon the whitewashed wall: “The killer is Wu Song, the Tiger Slayer.” He stamped the vessels on the table flat and stuffed several into his bosom. He was just about to go downstairs when he heard the lady below call, “The gentlemen upstairs are all drunk. Send two men quickly to help them down!” Before she had finished speaking, two men were already coming upstairs. Wu Song slipped beside the staircase and looked: they were two personal attendants, the very men who had seized him the other day. Hidden in the darkness, Wu Song let them pass, then blocked their retreat. The two entered the upper room and saw three corpses sprawled in pools of blood. They stared at each other in speechless terror, as though “the crowns of their skulls had split into eight pieces and half a bucket of icy water had been poured through them.” Just as they were about to turn, Wu Song came up behind them. His hand rose, his blade fell, and one man was cut down at once. The other dropped to his knees and begged for mercy. Wu Song said, “You are not one I can spare!” He seized him and cut off his head too. Blood spattered the painted tower, and corpses lay beneath the lamplight. Wu Song said, “In for a penny, in for a pound. Even if I kill a hundred, I can die only once.” Sword in hand, he went downstairs.

p.src: The lady asked, “What is all that commotion upstairs?” Wu Song rushed to the front of her room. Seeing a huge man approaching, she still asked, “Who are you?” Wu Song's sword was already flying. It struck her full in the face, and she fell before the room crying out in pain. Wu Song pinned her down and tried to cut off her head, but the blade would not bite through her neck. Puzzled, Wu Song examined the sword in the moonlight and saw that its edge was already entirely notched. Wu Song said, “No wonder I cannot cut off her head!” He withdrew through the rear door to fetch his long-handled sword, threw away the notched blade, and turned back into the ground floor. By the light of a lamp, he saw Yulan, the singing girl from before, leading two maidservants. The lamp revealed the lady lying murdered on the floor, and Yulan had only just cried, “Oh, misery!” Gripping the long-handled sword, Wu Song thrust it into Yulan's heart. Wu Song stabbed the two maidservants to death as well, dispatching each with a single thrust of the long-handled sword. He went out into the central hall and barred the front gate. Then he came back inside, found another two or three women, and stabbed them all to death in their rooms.

p.src: Wu Song said, “Only now am I fully satisfied. Time to leave!” He discarded the scabbard, took up the long-handled sword, and went out through the side gate. In the stable yard he took down a carrying pouch, put the flattened silver wine vessels from his bosom inside, tied it about his waist, then strode away with the weapon held point-down behind him. At the edge of the city he thought, “If I wait for the gates to open, I am sure to be caught. Better to scale the wall and flee tonight. Thereupon he climbed up onto the wall from beside it. Mengzhou was a small place, and its earthen wall was not very high. Looking down from beside the battlements, he first tested the long-handled sword, holding its blade upward and its shaft downward; then he leapt, planted the shaft against the ground, and landed beside the moat. In the moonlight he saw that the water was only a foot or two deep. It was then the middle of the tenth month, when springs and streams everywhere had dried up. Beside the moat Wu Song removed his shoes and socks, untied his leggings and knee guards, hitched up his clothes, and waded through the city moat to the opposite bank. Then he remembered the pair of hemp sandals in the bundle Shi En had sent him, took them out, and put them on. Listening to the watch calls within the city, he heard that it was already the third beat of the fourth watch. Wu Song said, “Only today have I finally vented this damned anger. ‘Fine though Liang Garden may be, it is no home in which to linger.’ I must make myself scarce.” Taking up his long-handled sword, he set off along a small road leading east. p.src: Intent on drawing his blade upon the road, he still rejoiced to drink wine in the tower. One man brought ruin upon many; more dreadful than his killing hand was his murderous heart. Yet had the wronged ghosts entwined themselves about him, how could he ever have slipped away?

p.src: He walked on until the fifth watch; the sky was dim and hazy, not yet bright. After the hardships of the night, Wu Song's body was exhausted; the wounds from his beating had begun to ache again, and he could endure no more. Seeing a tiny old temple in a grove, Wu Song hurried inside, leaned his long-handled sword against the wall, took down his bundle to use as a pillow, threw himself down, and went to sleep. Just as he was closing his eyes, two hooked poles reached in from outside the temple and caught hold of him. Two people rushed in, pinned Wu Song down, and bound him with a rope. The four men and women said, “This damned fellow is plump. He will make a fine gift for our elder brother.” Wu Song could not struggle free. The four took his bundle and long-handled sword and, as though dragging a sheep, hauled him off to the village with his feet barely touching the ground. As they went, the four men and women said among themselves, “Look at all the blood on this fellow. Where can he have come from? Could he be a thief who botched his job?” Wu Song said nothing and let them talk. After traveling no more than three or five li, they soon reached a thatched house and shoved Wu Song inside. Inside a small side door a bowl lamp was still burning. The four men and women stripped Wu Song and tied him to a pavilion post. Looking about, Wu Song saw two human legs hanging from a beam beside the stove. He thought to himself, “I have fallen into the hands of demons of violent death; now I shall die without anyone knowing what became of me. Had I known it would come to this, I would rather have surrendered myself at Mengzhou Prefecture. Even if I had suffered execution and dismemberment, at least I would have left an honorable name in the world.” Indeed:

p.src: Before the time needed to drink a cup of tea had passed, two people came in from the rear of the house. When Wu Song looked, he saw a woman in front and a burly man behind her. The two stared closely at Wu Song, and the woman cried, “Why, isn’t this our brother, Constable Wu!” The burly man said, “Quickly, untie my brother!” Wu Song looked again. The burly man was none other than Zhang Qing, the Vegetable Gardener, and the woman was Sun Erniang, the “Night Hag.” The four men and women were startled. They hastily loosened the ropes and dressed Wu Song in his clothes. His headcloth had already been torn to shreds, so they found a felt hat and put it on him. It turned out that Zhang Qing had several shops and workshops at Crossroads Slope, which was why Wu Song had not recognized this one. Zhang Qing immediately invited him into the guest room at the front, where they exchanged formal greetings. Greatly alarmed, Zhang Qing hurriedly asked, “Good brother, how did you come to be in such a state?” Wu Song replied, “It’s a long story! After parting from you, I reached the prison camp and met the commandant’s son, Shi En, known as the ‘Golden-Eyed Tiger Cub.’ He treated me like an old friend from our first meeting and provided me with good wine and meat every day. He owned a tavern and meat shop in Happy Grove east of the city, and it brought in a great deal of money; but a brute called Jiang the Gate God, whom Instructor Zhang had brought there, relied on his powerful connections and brazenly seized it from him for nothing. When Shi En told me this, I could not stand by in the face of injustice. I beat Jiang the Gate God while drunk and recovered Happy Grove, and for that Shi En held me in great esteem. Later, Instructor Zhang bribed Commandant Zhang. They devised a scheme in which the commandant took me into his personal service and cunningly framed me to avenge Jiang the Gate God. On the night of the fifteenth day of the eighth month, they falsely raised an alarm about a thief and lured me inside. They had already planted silver drinking vessels in my trunk. Then they seized me, sent me under guard to Mengzhou Prefecture, forced me to confess to theft under beating, and locked me in jail. He was generous and righteous and refused to frame an innocent man. And there was a jailer named Kang, who was a close friend of Shi En. The two of them did all they could to protect me. When the prescribed term was up, I received the cane across my back and was reassigned to Enzhou. Last night, after I left the city, that villain Commandant Zhang had laid another plot. He made Jiang the Gate God send two disciples to join the constables escorting me and finish me off along the road. When we reached a secluded spot at Flying Cloud Pool, they were just about to strike, but I kicked the two disciples into the water first. Then I caught up with those two cursed constables and stabbed each of them dead with the broad-bladed sword, tossing them both into the water. I wondered how else I could vent my rage, and so I turned back toward Mengzhou city. p.src: The four ruffians knelt and said, “All four of us are Brother Zhang’s companions. We’ve been losing at gambling for several days, so we went into the woods to look for some business. Then we saw you coming along the side path, dripping all over and covered in blood. You stopped to rest in the shrine of the local earth god, and we four had no idea who you were. Luckily, Brother Zhang has been telling us lately, ‘Only take them alive.’ That’s why we went out with nothing but grappling hooks and lassos. Had he not given that order, we would have cost you your life. Truly, we had eyes but failed to recognize Mount Tai. In our ignorance we offended you—please forgive us!” Zhang Qing and his wife laughed. “We had something on our minds, so lately we’ve ordered them to take only live merchandise. How could these four have understood what was in our hearts? If my brother here had not been exhausted, not merely you four men and women, but even forty of you could not have come near him.” The four ruffians kept knocking their heads against the floor. Wu Song bade them rise and said, “Since you have no money to gamble with, I’ll give you some.” He opened the bundle, took out ten taels of silver, and gave it to the four men to divide among themselves. The four ruffians bowed and thanked Wu Song. Seeing this, Zhang Qing also took out two or three taels of silver and rewarded the four, who went off to divide it among themselves.

If the victim proved less capable than they, they were to capture him alive; if they could not overcome him, they would inevitably have to kill him. For that reason I forbade them to carry blades and weapons, giving them only grappling hooks and lassos. When I heard their report just now, I became suspicious and hurriedly told them to wait until I came to look for myself. Who would have thought it truly was you!” Sun Erniang said, “As soon as people heard that you had beaten Jiang the Gate God—and defeated him while drunk at that—every traveler who passed this way was astonished! Merchants who did business at Happy Grove often spoke of it here, but we knew nothing of what happened afterward. You are exhausted. p.src: Now, some people in Commandant Zhang’s residence in Mengzhou had managed to hide and did not dare emerge until the fifth watch. They roused the personal attendants within and summoned the soldiers and constables on duty outside to inspect the scene. Though the alarm spread, who among the neighbors dared come out? They waited until daybreak, then went to the Mengzhou prefectural office to lodge a complaint. The prefect was greatly alarmed when he heard the report and immediately sent men to count the dead, investigate where the killer had entered and departed, and complete a diagram and itemized record. They returned and reported: “He first entered through the stables, where he killed a groom, and two discarded garments were found there. He next went to the kitchen hearth and killed two maidservants. A notched sword used in the murders was left beside the rear gate. Upstairs, Commandant Zhang and two personal attendants were killed. Also among the dead were the invited guests, Training Officer Zhang and Jiang the Door God. On a whitewashed wall, someone had dipped the hem of his robe in blood and written eight large characters: ‘The killer is Wu Song, the Tiger Slayer.’ Downstairs, the lady of the house was stabbed to death; outside, Yulan, her nurse, and three children were also stabbed to death. In all, fifteen men and women were killed, and six gold and silver drinking vessels were carried away.” After reading the report, the prefect immediately sent men to guard Mengzhou’s four gates; he mobilized troops and arresting officers and ordered the ward and neighborhood headmen throughout the city to search every house for the murderer Wu Song. The next day, the local headmen of Flying Cloud Pool reported: “Four men have been killed at the pool. Bloodstains from the killings are visible beneath the bridge, and all four bodies are in the water.” Upon receiving the complaint, the prefect assigned the county military magistrate to the case. He had the four bodies recovered from the water and examined them all. Two were constables of the prefecture, while the other two had relatives who claimed their bodies. Coffins were prepared and the corpses laid in them; all the bereaved parties then lodged complaints, pressing for the chief murderer’s arrest and execution. The city gates remained shut for three days while every family and household was investigated. Five households were made jointly responsible and ten formed a security group; there was nowhere they did not search. The prefect sealed official orders and appointed officers to search every district under their jurisdiction—every township, security group, borough, and village—house by house, to arrest the chief murderer. They recorded Wu Song’s native place, age, features, and appearance, issued his portrait, and offered a reward of three thousand strings of cash. Anyone who knew Wu Song’s whereabouts was to report to the prefecture and receive the stated reward; anyone who concealed the fugitive and gave him lodging or food would, upon discovery and prosecution, suffer the same penalty as the fugitive. The orders circulated throughout the neighboring prefectures and jurisdictions, which joined in the pursuit.

p.src: Meanwhile, Wu Song rested at Zhang Qing’s home for several days. He learned that the situation had become desperately urgent and that constables were streaming out of the city to search every village. When Zhang Qing heard this, he had no choice but to say to Wu Song: “Second Brother, it is not that I fear trouble or am unwilling to let you stay longer. But the authorities are searching so urgently, going from door to door, that if some mishap occurs tomorrow, you will surely resent my wife and me. I shall find you a safe refuge—the place I mentioned to you before—but I do not know whether you are truly willing to go.” Wu Song said: “I too have been thinking these past few days that this affair was certain to come to light. How could I remain safely settled here? I had only one elder brother, and he was murdered through my sister-in-law’s cruelty; and no sooner had I managed to come here than I was entrapped in this fashion. All my kin and relatives back home are gone. If you have a good refuge for me today and tell me to go there, how could I refuse? I merely wonder where it is.” Zhang Qing said: “It is the Precious Pearl Monastery on Twin Dragons Mountain, under the jurisdiction of Qingzhou. Lu Zhishen, the Flowery Monk, and that hero Yang Zhi, the Blue-Faced Beast, have taken possession of the region and become outlaws there, raiding homes and seizing property. The Qingzhou troops sent to suppress banditry do not even dare look them in the eye. Only by taking refuge there, worthy brother, can you escape this danger. If you go anywhere else, you will eventually be arrested. They often send letters inviting me to move there, but I am too attached to my native soil to leave and have never gone. I will write a letter describing all your exploits in detail. Out of regard for me, how could they refuse to admit you to their band?” Wu Song said: “What you say is right, Elder Brother. I have long had such an intention, but regrettably the time had not come and circumstances would not bring it about. Now that I have killed men, the affair has come to light, and I have nowhere to hide, this is the finest possible course. Elder Brother, write the letter for me, and I shall leave this very day.”

p.src: Zhang Qing immediately fetched a sheet of paper and wrote a detailed letter, which he gave to Wu Song, then prepared food and wine for his journey. But Sun Erniang, the She-Devil, pointed at Zhang Qing and said: “How can you simply send our brother off like this? He is certain to be arrested farther down the road.” Wu Song said: “Sister-in-law, tell me why I cannot go. Why should I be arrested?” Sun Erniang said: “Brother, the authorities have now circulated warrants everywhere, offering a reward of three thousand strings of cash. They have drawn your likeness, clearly recorded your native place and age, and posted the notices wherever you might go. And the two lines of penal brands stand plainly on your face. Once you take to the road, there is no concealing them.” Zhang Qing said: “He need only put two medicinal plasters on his face.” Sun Erniang laughed. “You alone are clever under heaven! What foolish nonsense. How could that deceive the constables? I have a plan, though I fear our brother may not agree to it.” Wu Song said: “Since I must flee calamity and escape danger, why should I not agree?” Sun Erniang laughed heartily. “When I tell you, Brother, you must not take offense.” Wu Song said: “Whatever you say, Sister-in-law, I shall do.” Sun Erniang said: “Two years ago, a wandering Buddhist ascetic passed this way. p.src: Seeing that matters were growing urgent, Wu Song packed his bundle and prepared to leave. Zhang Qing said again, “Second Brother, hear me out. I am not trying to profit at your expense. Leave here the wine vessels you took from Commandant Zhang’s house. I shall exchange them for small pieces of silver to serve as your traveling expenses, and then nothing can go wrong.” Wu Song said, “Elder Brother sees the matter clearly.” He took them all out and gave them to Zhang Qing, who exchanged them for a packet of small pieces of gold and silver. Wu Song secured it all inside his money belt and tied it around his waist. Wu Song ate his fill of wine and food, took leave of Zhang Qing and his wife, and slung the two monastic swords at his waist. Everything was made ready that very evening. Sun Erniang brought out the ordination certificate, sewed a brocade pouch for it, and told Wu Song to hang it against his bare chest beneath his clothes. Wu Song bowed his thanks to the husband and wife. As he was about to depart, Zhang Qing admonished him once more: “Second Brother, take great care on the road and never be overconfident in anything. Drink less wine, do not quarrel or brawl with others, and conduct yourself somewhat as a man of religion should. Do not lose your temper over anything, lest someone see through your disguise. When you reach Two Dragon Mountain, write us a letter and send it back. For the two of us to remain here is no lasting solution either. Very likely we shall soon gather up our household goods and join the band on the mountain as well. Take good care of yourself, Second Brother, and be sure to convey our respects to the two chieftains, Lu and Yang.”

u.src: Seeing that matters were growing urgent, Wu Song packed his bundle and prepared to leave.

Zhang Qing said again, “Second Brother, hear me out. I am not trying to profit at your expense. Leave here the wine vessels you took from Commandant Zhang’s house. I shall exchange them for small pieces of silver to serve as your traveling expenses, and then nothing can go wrong.”
Wu Song said, “Elder Brother sees the matter clearly.”
He took them all out and gave them to Zhang Qing, who exchanged them for a packet of small pieces of gold and silver. Wu Song secured it all inside his money belt and tied it around his waist.
Wu Song ate his fill of wine and food, took leave of Zhang Qing and his wife, and slung the two monastic swords at his waist. Everything was made ready that very evening.
Sun Erniang brought out the ordination certificate, sewed a brocade pouch for it, and told Wu Song to hang it against his bare chest beneath his clothes.
Wu Song bowed his thanks to the husband and wife.
As he was about to depart, Zhang Qing admonished him once more: “Second Brother, take great care on the road and never be overconfident in anything.
Drink less wine, do not quarrel or brawl with others, and conduct yourself somewhat as a man of religion should.
Do not lose your temper over anything, lest someone see through your disguise.
When you reach Two Dragon Mountain, write us a letter and send it back.
For the two of us to remain here is no lasting solution either.
Very likely we shall soon gather up our household goods and join the band on the mountain as well.
Take good care of yourself, Second Brother, and be sure to convey our respects to the two chieftains, Lu and Yang.”

p.src: Wu Song took his leave and went out, thrust his hands into the opposite sleeves, and strode away with a swagger. Watching him, Zhang Qing and his wife applauded and cried, “What a splendid wandering monk he makes!” Behold: the hair in front shaded his brows, while the uneven locks behind reached the nape of his neck. His black robe was like a dark cloud enveloping his body, and his motley sash like a flowered python coiled about him. The gleaming metal band upon his brow gave him something of the Fiery-Eyed, Golden-Pupiled One; the many-colored patched jacket about his body made him seem sinewed with bronze and boned with iron. Two monastic swords, which when raised spread murderous fury through the autumn air; a rosary of a hundred skull-bones, which when counted filled the road with mournful winds. Man-eating rakshasas must fold their hands before him, and even Dharma-guarding vajra warriors would knit their brows.

p.src: That evening, “Wu the Pilgrim” bade farewell to Zhang Qing and his wife, left the Great Tree Crossroads, and set out upon the road. It was then the tenth month, when the days were short, and evening fell in the blink of an eye. After traveling not quite fifty li, he could already see a lofty ridge ahead. By the bright moonlight, “Wu the Pilgrim” climbed the ridge step by step, reckoning that it was only around the first watch. Standing atop the ridge, Wu the Pilgrim looked out and saw the moon rising in the east, bathing all the grass and trees upon the heights in radiance. As he watched, he suddenly heard someone laughing in the woods ahead. “Wu the Pilgrim” said, “More devilry! Who could be laughing and talking on such an utterly deserted ridge?” He crossed to the far side of the woods to investigate. There in the pine forest, beside the mountainside, stood a hermitage by a graveyard, comprising some dozen thatched rooms. Two small windows stood open, and before them a religious master was embracing a woman as they gazed at the moon, laughing and sporting together. At the sight, anger rose in “Wu the Pilgrim’s” heart and malice sprang beside his gall. He thought, “This man is a recluse dwelling amid the mountain forests, yet he engages in such business!” He drew from his waist the two monastic swords that shone like tarnished silver. Examining them in the moonlight, he said, “The blades are fine indeed, but since coming into my hands they have yet to make their first sale. I shall try their edge on this damned master.” He suspended one blade from his wrist, returned the other to its sheath, knotted the two sleeves of his robe behind his back, and went straight to the hermitage door and knocked. Hearing the noise, the master immediately shut the rear window. “Wu the Pilgrim” picked up a stone and began battering the door. With a creak, a side door opened and a Daoist acolyte came out. He shouted, “Who are you? How dare you raise such an uproar in the dead of night, pounding and beating on our door? What do you want?” “Wu the Pilgrim” opened his fierce eyes wide and roared, “First I shall sacrifice this damned acolyte to my blade!” Before he had finished speaking, his hand rose and there came a ringing clang. The acolyte’s head fell to one side and his body collapsed to the ground. Then the master inside the hermitage shouted, “Who dares kill my acolyte?” With a bound, he leaped out. Brandishing two precious swords, the master charged straight at “Wu the Pilgrim.” Wu Song laughed loudly and said, “There is no need to fetch my skill from a box—you have struck precisely where I itch!” He drew the other monastic sword from its sheath, whirled both blades, and went to meet the master. Beneath the bright moon the two advanced and retreated, moved in and out; the pair of swords flashed with icy light, while the twin monastic blades breathed a chilling air. They fought for a long while, like a flying phoenix meeting a luan bird; before much more time had passed, it was like a horned hawk seizing a hare. After they had exchanged more than ten bouts, a loud crash suddenly sounded beside the ridge, and one of the two fell. Behold, amid cold gleaming shadows a human head fell; within the gathering murderous air, a rain of blood burst forth. Which of the two combatants was it who fell? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
